notes: Each eval feeds the reviewer a realistic planted-bug diff for the Naglasúpan repo. The fixtures live in fixtures/*.diff. The point is to test whether the skill catches REPO-SPECIFIC issues a generic review misses, while not raising noise. Baseline runs (no skill) are expected to catch generic issues but miss the house-convention ones.

evals.name: frontend-transient-logout-regression
evals.prompt: I'm about to merge a change to the Naglasúpan repo at /home/siggi/sources/nglspn. Can you review it before I do? The full diff is in the attached file. Tell me what a senior engineer on this project would flag.
evals.expected_output: Flags that the change now clears tokens / logs the user out on TRANSIENT refresh failures (network blip, 5xx), not just genuine 'invalid' credential failures — a known regression class in this repo (#61/#64). Should treat this as a blocker or important. Should NOT demand api-types.ts regeneration (no API change here).

assertions.text: Identifies that the change logs users out on transient/network/5xx refresh failures, not just real auth failures
Explains the concrete user-facing consequence (spurious logout on a network blip / backend hiccup)
Rates it at least Important/Blocker severity rather than a minor nit
Does NOT raise false positives about formatting, imports, or the absent api-types.ts

evals.name: backend-xff-ip-spoof
evals.prompt: Quick review before I merge this to /home/siggi/sources/nglspn please — the diff is attached. Anything concerning?
evals.expected_output: Flags that switching to the FIRST (leftmost) X-Forwarded-For entry lets a client forge its IP and bypass the rate limit, since the leftmost entries are attacker-controlled. Should reference taking the rightmost / trusted-proxy-aware value (NUM_TRUSTED_PROXIES) and treat it as a security blocker.

assertions.text: Identifies that the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value is client-controlled and therefore spoofable
Explains the consequence: an attacker can bypass the rate limit by forging the header
References the correct approach (rightmost entry / NUM_TRUSTED_PROXIES / trusted proxy count)
Treats it as a security blocker / high severity

evals.name: backend-api-pii-and-contract
evals.prompt: Here's a new endpoint I added to the Naglasúpan backend (repo at /home/siggi/sources/nglspn) — a public profile route. The diff is attached. Review it as if you were the senior engineer approving the PR.
evals.expected_output: Should catch multiple repo-specific issues: (1) kennitala (Icelandic national ID / PII) is returned to ANY caller for ANY user — a privacy blocker; (2) the API/schema changed but backend-openapi.json was not regenerated/committed, so the frontend contract is stale; (3) the endpoint has no auth and no ownership/visibility check, and uses inline User.objects.get (raises DoesNotExist -> 500 instead of the declared 404) instead of going through REPO. Should NOT complain that api-types.ts is missing (it is gitignored).

assertions.text: Flags that kennitala (PII / national ID) is exposed to arbitrary callers
Flags that backend-openapi.json was not regenerated despite an API/schema change
Flags the missing authorization (no auth=auth) and/or missing ownership/visibility check on the endpoint
Notes the inline User.objects.get bypasses the REPO services layer and/or raises DoesNotExist (500) instead of the declared 404
Does NOT incorrectly flag the absence of api-types.ts (it is gitignored)
